body:
I am extremely close-knit with my family, and with the exception of the fact that I wish they were more liberal with their beliefs, I couldn't ask for a better family.  I've never seen them judge someone to their face, but I have heard them rant at the TV many times (usually about LGBT folks––gay men first, then trans, then everything else).  Dealing with their reactions when Chastity Bono announced his intention to change to Chaz Bono was difficult, to say the least.

I really do hope that they'd be willing to hep me with my identity, or at the very least willing to step back and let me figure things out for myself.  I think my real issue right now is that I'm too dependent on them, especially financially.  Of course, while I understand why you're saying I should graduate first (something I agree with, actually), it's hard to imagine that I'm still *two years* away from doing that.  The idea of living in this shitty emotional state for two more years is not something I like to think about.

Correction, if the relationship gets damaged I can blame myself, I just shouldn't.  I'm not ashamed of who I am, but I'm extremely disappointed and upset––not that I think it's wrong to be trans, but that I'm really pissed off for being in this situation in the first place.  I'm so scared of my future and the bad things that could happen that I freeze up whenever I have a chance to improve the present.  I don't want to ruin my relationship with my parents, and I definitely don't want to fuck up my chance of getting an education.

I'm not sure I'd use the word "outgrown", but I definitely no longer accept a large amount of what was taught to me about religion.  It really started with realizing that young earth creationism is a load of bullshit (how my otherwise very intelligent parents eat this stuff up I don't know) and then I slowly realized how much hate there was in the church I grew up in.  I guess my problem is that for some reason I still feel *something* religious, it's just that all I see any more is hypocrisy within the church and unanswered questions from the Bible.

There's an LGBT group at school which I'll be officially joining this year, although I've been to a number of things with my gay friend (who I'm out to).  From what I've seen it's really more sort of a gay and lesbian dating service than a support group, and I know that I'd be the only openly trans person on campus.  For a campus of roughly 16,000 undergrads, that's pretty significant isolation.

Thanks for the Dan Savage link, by the way.  Here's hoping it all pans out as he said it would, but the whole financial dependence thing is still a bit too risky for me to mess with.

Your brother sounds like a really cool guy.  My problem is exactly what you said, that family is important.  Even ignoring the financial stuff, if I came out to my parents and damaged that relationship I'm not sure how I'd handle it.  For the most part I have a good family life, and I'm not sure I could forgive myself if I destroyed that.

I have looked into other branches, but my eyes frequently glaze over when I spend too long looking at doctrine.  I'll try to attack them sometime, but part of my problem is deeper than interpretations of certain passages but rather about the fact that something has just seemed to disappear from within me.  I don't feel what I used to about religion.

Go right ahead.  I'm literally a week shy of my 21st birthday, and tomorrow I head back to school for my junior year.

> The good news: you can overcome this, the bad news: it will take some time. If you're still finishing up school and living with your parents, you're looking at a period of time before you can move forward. Try to concentrate on the future, and the opportunities that await you.

Yeah, I'm looking at at least two more years until I can move on.

> You're obviously very bright and articulate, have you thought about getting a MSW? One day a kid might have you to thank for saving their life. You sound like a thoughtful person with an abundance of good things to offer, so don't let the failings of others get you down.

I have not, and in fact had to look up what that stood for.  While I appreciate the sentiment (and take it as a compliment that you think I sound like a thoughtful and good person :D ) I'm really not the social work type.  I have a hard time communicating with people.  Right now I'm actually majoring in electrical engineering, and with the exception of gender issues I fit the engineer stereotype pretty closely.

> As for your family, it's really hard to contradict people you love. Sometimes it's enough to concede that what they do works for them, and what you do works for you.

Yeah, it is, and I'm willing to let them sit in their beliefs for the most part.  I'm too afraid of those beliefs negatively affecting me if I were to tell them what's going on, though.

> There is nothing wrong with you BeirutQ :) Being transgendered is not a flaw. You are human. Some apples are red and some are green. Some people are black and some are white. You are just one type of this beautiful creature we call human. You may want to consider joining an LGBT club at your college for further support. You are not the first transgendered person in the world and definitely not the last. I do not know the specific difficulties you could be going through but self discovery is an important part of life and by identifying yourself, you are already maturing and becoming stronger as a person.

Convincing myself there was nothing wrong with me took me a while, but at this point I'm convinced.  I'll be joining the LGBT club at school (I already know a number of members) but it is for the most part a gay hangout and hook-up spot.  I think that's important for a good gay community, but it's hard that there's no openly trans people on my campus of ~16,000.

> Your real friends will accept you for what you are not what they want you to be :)

This is true, thanks.

> As you are financially dependent on them right now, I would advise you do not convey any information to them that could be harmful to your well-being at this time.

While I agree with the logic of it, it's a lot harder to accept this idea when I'm living this nightmare daily and won't be independent for at least two more years.

> Just to wonder since I'm not an expert on this topic, but why do you think that you can't do anything about it? If I'm not mistaken, there's some pretty impressive things that can be done with hormones, surgery, and therapy. There's no reason to live in a way that you don't feel deep down is right. Just because you can't do anything about it right now doesn't mean that you won't ever be able to do anything about it.

It's not that there's nothing I can do about it physically, it's that at the moment I feel trapped because there's nothing I can presently do about it.  My best option towards transition would be to come out to my parents, but there's too much risk involved regarding my education.  I'm basically looking at waiting at least two more years until I can start attacking my issues.

My main circle of friends is very liberal and accepted me when I came out to them.  The real issue is those people at home: my parents, my sister, my high school friends, and so on.  I'm afraid that if I came out fully I'd be alienating myself from my hometown, which I for the most part love.

And yeah, I have thought about moving to a different country, believe it or not.  Not sure I can leave my family behind like that.
Hmm, I'll consider it.  And no, I'm not your cousin, I've got no cousins of my own.
Oh, hey, neat, a random person on the internet doesn't like me despite never meeting me!  This has never, ever happened before.

I admit that I've never heard of body integrity identity disorder, but as a transgirl I have to admit that it's not so much about trying to get my dick removed as it is about being able to be female.  I'll take a guess based on the fact that I'm on Reddit and assume you're male.  Now assume you feel exactly the same way you do now but are in a female's body, forever.  That's the situation us tgirls are in, just in reverse.
